steps.text:
I couldn't list the droplets. The gateway allowed the call to `digitalocean/droplet-list`, but DigitalOcean's API rejected it with **401 "Unable to authenticate you"** (request ID `1defecf3-064b-4e0a-a8f3-f9eddb436285`).

The likely cause is the setup, not a permissions rule. The DigitalOcean connection is set up with a placeholder API token (`DIGITALOCEAN_API_TOKEN=dummy-not-a-real-credential`), so it can't log in to the account. No droplet data came back, so I can't give you any droplet names, IDs or counts.

To fix this, someone with admin access to the gateway needs to replace that placeholder with a valid DigitalOcean API token that has read access to droplets. Once that's done, I can run the request again.
